title: Wine Wimsey Review · Fri Nov 6
subtitle: 16 feed posts (all images, no TOBIs) and 4 stories. Posting date is Fri Nov 6 (next unused folder after Nov 5); if you meant Nov 7, say so. Inbox: no new items, none used. Held posts: 0. Test cells at queue positions 2, 6, 10, 14: B (#2, plain card), C (#6, Hot Mess image, edgy quote), D (#10, plain card), A (#14, Homebody image). No caption or first comment on any of them. Seasonal: 6 regular feed posts (#1, #4, #7, #11, #13, #16) plus story 1. Characters: Hot Mess 12 posts, Homebody 5 (incl. 2 stories). FLAG: only 8 evergreen regular quotes exist after taking 6 seasonal, so the 4th/11th non-seasonal rule can't apply; A and B are the two extra evergreen quotes written in the usual style (a Homebody image and a card). Credits: 810 for 18 images at 1K/low/4:5 (first try, nothing regenerated); the 2 cards cost none. Test C has the word 'shit' (edgy cell, per plan).

posts.quote: MY THANKSGIVING MENU FITS ON ONE INDEX CARD. THE FAMILY HAS ASKED FOR A SECOND CARD. THE CARD HAS SAID NO.
posts.caption: I wrote the whole menu on one index card and felt very organized for about an hour. Then the requests started coming in. Somebody wants the green bean thing. Somebody else wants the other green bean thing. The card is full and I have stopped reading texts.
posts.first: I found a second index card in the junk drawer and put it back. A boundary can be small and still count.
posts.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun at a kitchen counter holding up a crowded index card and shaking her head, with a glass of red wine and autumn leaves in the window. Text at the top reads: My Thanksgiving menu fits on one index card. The family has asked for a second card. The card has said no.

posts.quote: I can do anything for an hour. Then I need to lie down and review my choices.
posts.alt: Plain off-white card with dark bold text. Text reads: I can do anything for an hour. Then I need to lie down and review my choices.

posts.quote: NOBODY WARNS YOU THAT YOUR FAVORITE CHAIR WILL EVENTUALLY BE THE ONE YOU CAN'T GET OUT OF.
posts.caption: I used to pick a chair by how it looked. Now I pick one by how the exit works. This one has been in the family room for eleven years and we have an understanding. It holds me gently and lets me go in its own time.
posts.first: I got up to answer the door yesterday and it took two tries and a small speech. The delivery guy waited. I tipped him with a nod.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a plump woman with short mauve-pink curls sunk deep into a floral armchair, holding a wine glass and looking content and stuck. Text at the top reads: Nobody warns you that your favorite chair will eventually be the one you can't get out of.

posts.quote: IT'S 41 DEGREES OUT AND I WALKED TO THE CAR IN SLIPPERS TO SAVE TIME. I SAVED NO TIME.
posts.caption: The forecast said 41 and I believed it with my whole chest, and then I went out in slippers anyway. The car was thirty feet away. Thirty feet is longer in November. I arrived with cold toes and a new respect for shoes.
posts.first: The slippers are fine, by the way. They went back to the door and sat there looking sorry.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun in fuzzy slippers hurrying across a frosty driveway toward a parked car with her breath showing in the cold. Text at the top reads: It's 41 degrees out and I walked to the car in slippers to save time. I saved no time.

posts.quote: MY MOTHER SAID I'D REGRET NOT WEARING A COAT. I'M 53 AND STILL SITTING IN THE CAR TO FINISH THAT ARGUMENT.
posts.caption: My mother said it would be cold and I said I'd be fine. That was in the driveway. I'm now in the car with the heat on, decided, and it's been eight minutes. Some arguments you finish alone, with the seat warmer.
posts.first: She called later and asked how the weather was. I said mild. We both knew.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sitting in a parked car with the heater on, arms crossed, looking stubborn and a little chilly. Text at the top reads: My mother said I'd regret not wearing a coat. I'm 53 and still sitting in the car to finish that argument.

posts.quote: I'VE STARTED SAYING "BACK IN MY DAY" ABOUT SHIT THAT HAPPENED LAST SPRING.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun gesturing dramatically with a wine glass in a living room as if telling a story. Text at the top reads: I've started saying back in my day about shit that happened last spring.

posts.quote: THERE'S A HOLE IN THE ELBOW OF MY SWEATER AND IT'S THE ONLY ONE THAT FEELS LIKE A HUG. WE'RE STAYING TOGETHER.
posts.caption: There's a hole in the elbow of this sweater that's been getting bigger since last winter. I've considered replacing it. The new ones have never once loved me back. This one knows where the couch is.
posts.first: I put my finger through the hole while I was reading and it felt like the sweater saying hello. I'm keeping it another year.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a plump woman with short mauve-pink curls in an ochre knit sweater poking a finger through a hole in the elbow while cuddled in a floral chair with a wine glass nearby. Text at the top reads: There's a hole in the elbow of my sweater and it's the only one that feels like a hug. We're staying together.

posts.quote: I KEEP THE SUBTITLES ON BECAUSE EVERYONE IN MOVIES MUMBLES NOW. IT'S NOT ME. I'VE CHECKED WITH THE SUBTITLES.
posts.caption: I turned the subtitles on in March and haven't looked back. Nobody in the shows speaks up anymore. They lean in and whisper like the plot is a secret. The subtitles and I are on the same page, which is the only page I read all evening.
posts.first: My niece said it's the sound mixing. I told her that's what I've been saying and we agreed to leave it there.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a plump woman with short mauve-pink curls on a sofa with a bowl of popcorn, pointing at a TV screen that shows subtitles. Text at the top reads: I keep the subtitles on because everyone in movies mumbles now. It's not me. I've checked with the subtitles.

posts.quote: I REACHED FOR THE TOP SHELF AND MY SHOULDER SAID 'WE'RE DONE HERE.' NOW I EAT WHAT'S ON THE MIDDLE SHELF.
posts.caption: The top shelf used to be for the things I use most. Now it's for the things I'm pretending I own. I reached for the big pot, my shoulder said no with a small noise, and I decided soup comes in a mug anyway.
posts.first: I bought a step stool. It's currently being used to hold a plant. The shoulder and I are both fine with that.
posts.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun in a kitchen reaching for a high cabinet shelf with one arm and wincing, a wine glass on the counter. Text at the top reads: I reached for the top shelf and my shoulder said 'We're done here.' Now I eat what's on the middle shelf.

posts.quote: I don't say "no" to plans anymore. I say "let me check" and never check.
posts.alt: Plain off-white card with dark bold text. Text reads: I don't say "no" to plans anymore. I say "let me check" and never check.

posts.quote: THANKSGIVING IS THREE WEEKS AWAY AND I'VE BEEN SAYING 'WE'LL SEE' ABOUT THE SWEET POTATOES SINCE HALLOWEEN.
posts.caption: Thanksgiving is three weeks off and I've been saying 'we'll see' about the sweet potatoes since Halloween. Marshmallows or no marshmallows is a debate I'm not entering again. Whoever shows up with a casserole can have the opinion.
posts.first: I've bought the sweet potatoes. They're in the pantry looking confident. I haven't committed to anything else.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun in a grocery store aisle holding a sweet potato in one hand and a bag of marshmallows in the other, looking undecided. Text at the top reads: Thanksgiving is three weeks away and I've been saying 'we'll see' about the sweet potatoes since Halloween.

posts.quote: THE COMPRESSION SOCKS SAID EASY TO WEAR. FOUR MINUTES FOR ONE SOCK. I'M COUNTING IT AS CARDIO.
posts.caption: The package said easy to wear. It was written by someone with young shoulders and no fear of the bed. Four minutes for one sock, a rest, and then I started the second. I'm counting it as my cardio and I'm still on the edge of the bed.
posts.first: They work, though. My ankles stopped sending reports. I put the second one on while sitting on the stairs like a person with a plan.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a flushed woman with a messy grey-streaked bun sitting on the edge of a bed straining to pull a long compression sock over her foot. Text at the top reads: The compression socks said easy to wear. Four minutes for one sock. I'm counting it as cardio.

posts.quote: NINE DAYS IN THE SAME FLEECE AND IT'S STARTING TO FEEL LIKE A SECOND SKIN. THE FIRST ONE IS GETTING JEALOUS.
posts.caption: Nine days in the same fleece and it's the best I've ever felt in clothing. It's soft in places clothing shouldn't be soft. The laundry basket is looking at me. I told it I'm a free spirit and it should look elsewhere.
posts.first: I did wash it once. It was back on by dinner. It's like it never left, which is the entire point of the fleece.
posts.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun wearing a fluffy grey fleece zipped to her chin, hugging herself happily beside an overflowing laundry basket. Text at the top reads: Nine days in the same fleece and it's starting to feel like a second skin. The first one is getting jealous.

posts.quote: I'VE STARTED TALKING TO THE BIRDS AT THE FEEDER LIKE COWORKERS. THE CARDINAL IS LATE AGAIN.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a plump woman with short mauve-pink curls in a robe and slippers at a kitchen window with a mug of coffee, waving at a red cardinal on a bird feeder outside. Text at the top reads: I've started talking to the birds at the feeder like coworkers. The cardinal is late again.

posts.quote: I SAID I'D TAKE UP YOGA. I BOUGHT THE MAT. THE CAT NOW OWNS A VERY EXPENSIVE FLOOR RUNNER.
posts.caption: I'm going to start yoga on Monday. I've been saying that since March, and I have a lovely mat. It's purple. The cat discovered it in April and has been practicing ever since. She's very flexible and deeply uninterested in my progress.
posts.first: I did unroll it for her this morning. She did the full downward cat and then fell asleep on my goal.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun standing in a living room looking at a purple yoga mat where an orange cat is stretched out asleep. Text at the top reads: I said I'd take up yoga. I bought the mat. The cat now owns a very expensive floor runner.

posts.quote: THE STORE WAS PLAYING SLEIGH BELLS BEFORE I FINISHED MY CANDY CORN. I'M NOT READY TO BE RUSHED.
posts.caption: The store was playing sleigh bells while I stood in front of the candy corn in the first week of November. I had a cart and an open mind and then the song about chestnuts started, and I wasn't ready. I'm still on autumn, thank you.
posts.first: I bought the candy corn anyway. It was half off and the bells were already playing for the next display.
posts.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun in a store aisle holding a bag of candy corn, covering one ear and frowning at a speaker on the ceiling beside a display of Christmas ornaments. Text at the top reads: The store was playing sleigh bells before I finished my candy corn. I'm not ready to be rushed.

stories.quote: I PUT 'CLEAN THE OVEN' ON THE THANKSGIVING LIST. THE OVEN AND I HAVE AGREED TO DISAGREE.
stories.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun in oven mitts peering skeptically into a dirty oven, holding a wine glass. Text at the top reads: I put 'clean the oven' on the Thanksgiving list. The oven and I have agreed to disagree.

stories.quote: I LEFT THE HOUSE WITH ONE ERRAND AND A FULL PHONE BATTERY. I RETURNED WITH NEITHER.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a worn-out woman with a messy grey-streaked bun slumped in a doorway holding a phone showing an empty battery and an empty hand where a list should be. Text at the top reads: I left the house with one errand and a full phone battery. I returned with neither.

stories.quote: I'M NOT ANTISOCIAL. I'M JUST PROTECTING THE EVENING.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a plump woman with short mauve-pink curls relaxing on a sofa with a blanket and wine glass, with a door locked behind her. Text at the top reads: I'm not antisocial. I'm just protecting the evening.

stories.quote: MY ELECTRIC BLANKET HAS TEN SETTINGS. I USE ONE. IT'S CALLED SURRENDER.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a plump woman with short mauve-pink curls buried in a bed with a heated blanket and a controller, looking blissfully surrendered. Text at the top reads: My electric blanket has ten settings. I use one. It's called surrender.
